listing.aiSummary: Runs automated battles between factions to measure their balance.

description:
For a while, I've been curious about just how balanced StarSector's factions were. Accordingly, I stitched together an automated simulator that could run a large number of battles in sequence, with minimal resources, and aggregate the results.

Methodology:

This mod operates by running a bit over 300 matches at maximally-accelerated speed, with rendering pared down as much as I could. I'm not an experienced modder, so if there's a better way to build this, please let me know.

As far as the actual matches, I've aimed to be as fair as possible to the factions' builds, ignoring things that may vary over the course of the campaign, such as ship quality modifiers. In practice, this means:

All ships have zero D-mods, and all fleets have 240 DP worth of ships.
Because ship quality and fleet size are fixed, the officer quality setting is fixed as well, and set to 5 for all factions.
Fleets spawn in in the top and bottom, with no objectives. The admiral AI's handling of objectives is wonky enough that I kept it out of the initial run.
Retreat is disabled, as there's no clean way to represent it in the statistics.

I consider these to be reasonably defensible settings, but I encourage others to raise issues and replicate this work with any changes they consider beneficial to its overall validity.

Results:

I collect two metrics. The first is the win-loss ratio for each pairing, and the second is the ratio of deployment points destroyed. The latter is finer-grained, and lets us discern whether one faction just happens to have a better capital that can turn the tide, or whether matches are a complete stomp. Still, they tend to tell the same broad story.

Win-Loss Ratio:

We see, here, that the Hegemony gets far and away the strongest builds. They beat their arch-rivals, the League, 11 out of 12 times, and defeat the Independents, Diktat, and Tri-Tachyon three quarters of the time. They never once lose to the Church, Path, or Pirates.

After them come the League, who are well above everyone except the Hegemony. Their missile/fighter spam doctrine is indeed very effective, but, curiously, the Hegemony hard-counters it. You'd think it'd be the other way around, with a League hyper-specialized around defeating the Hegemony.

The Diktat, Tri-Tachyon, and Independents form the middle ranks, with the Diktat leading but no qualitative edge. Independents generally do better than Tri-Tachyon overall, but Tri-Tachyon beats independents very reliably. Diktat beats both, but not very reliably. I think Tri-Tachyon's big problem is that its AI is set to cautious, but its ships are all built for close-range engagements. Re-running TT-related tests with an aggressive AI would be a good followup.

Finally, the bottom tier has the Church, Path, and Pirates. I should reiterate that D-mods are not a factor here. The Path's underperformance surprised me quite a bit, given that SO is a powerful hullmod, and they have it built into almost everything. My best guesses are that the built-in D-mod on most of their ships was especially painful when everyone else had pristine ships, or that their lower-end fodder ships effectively acted as a handicap.

Entertainingly, the Path punched above its weight against their two biggest enemies, Tri-Tachyon and the Sindrian Diktat. The Pirates beat them more often than not, which I wouldn't have expected.

Ratios of DP Destroyed:

We see a few subtleties here, I won't reiterate anything in the above section. Bullet points:

Hegemony reliably achieves 2:1 or better kill ratios, which is pretty shocking. I expected them to come out on top, but not by this much. Oddly enough, Tri-Tachyon does the best against them, despite their builds appearing as though they were designed to counter high tech most of all.
League's kill ratios are similarly lopsided. It absolutely thrashes Tri-Tachyon, with a 5:1 ratio, which I wouldn't have expected early on, given that DEMs' core weakness is good shields, which TT has in abundance. My best guess is that DEM spam overwhelms and pops the shields of smaller TT ships at the start, producing a very lopsided fight later on.
The rest of the factions are relatively even in terms of kill ratios, varying from 0.5 to 2.0 at the extremes, but rarely going that far. My assertion is that their doctrines are somewhat incoherent, and they ultimately just trade ships until someone comes out ahead.

Analysis (and implications for game design):

When I started this, I expected more 'loops', rather than a strict, hierarchical power scale. I expected, for instance, that the Hegemony's kinetic-filled arsenal would result in lopsided fights against Tri-Tachyon, while Tri-Tach would be able to beat League reliably by no-selling DEMs' soft flux damage with their shields. Pathers would prey on Independents' relatively fragile, speedy vessels that depend on creating distance, while being beaten up reliably by factions with anchors that can push them back. This would add substantial depth to the game, with factions appearing to design their doctrines around enemies they expect to face at scale. A Hegemony player would need to watch out around the League, since they've been planning for years for this fight, but could readily kill Tri-Tachyon fleets because that's what his ships and weapons are set up to do.

Instead, we see a very strict, very linear power hierarchy. Hegemony >> League >> Diktat ~ Independent ~ Tri-Tachyon ~ Church > Path ~ Pirates. The loops we do see are relatively subdued, and light on lore implications. Tri-Tachyon underperforms against the Independents despite being above them by one place overall. Pirates (surprisingly) beat Pathers despite being one step below them. The Diktat underperforms against the Path despite a gap of four places, but that's the opposite of the way it's 'supposed' to be going - the Diktat's fleets are specialized for suppression and anti-piracy duty, while the Path's ships are meant to extort independent traders.

Some things I would try out:

Tri-Tach really underperforms, and badly. I think some of that comes from their cautious AI being paired with very aggressive ship builds. I'd expect that changing their AI to aggressive would make a big difference. Beyond that, some of their ship builds are really wacky, and could use a revisit.
The League's doctrine is extremely counterintuitive and anti-synergistic. They spam fighters to saturate PD and then use missiles that avoid PD. They're supposed to be fighting heavily-armored opponents, but their weapons are all energy-based, instead of HE. I'm not sure what I'd change to fix this; the DEMs are kind of baked in, so I'd lean towards reducing their use of fighters, which Hegemony PD instagibs anyhow.
The Diktat did better than I thought it would, but the fact that it loses reliably to the League despite having a heavily-shielded capital armed with two anti-fighter missile launchers in all of its fleets (and often more than one) is worth examining. Their Executors tend to go it alone and get surrounded, so a quick admiral script that ensures they always have a Centurion on their backs would probably help. Besides that, I'd switch them to steady AI since all of their ships are built to kite enemies. That's probably be a lot of free alpha.
Pirates and Pathers sitting at the bottom even when D-mods and officers are evened out feels like a missed opportunity. I'd like to see later-game versions of those factions that don't field any of the fodder ships and have hull-restored IAM away. I bet they'd do better.
The Luddic Church comes out well below the other three minor factions, which I think is somewhat due to the same issue, but also because of anti-synergy in their builds. You can't make a good AI fleet out of a Retribution and an Invictus; the former will rush in and get killed without support, and the latter will slowly move in and get surrounded by an enemy that now outnumbers it. They're the only 'normal' faction that uses deliberately bad fodder ships like the Cerberus, which hurts them a lot, but I think splitting them up into an attrition doctrine and a rush doctrine, and moving their ships around accordingly, would make a big difference. Moras and Invictuses could form a pretty solid wall, and Retributions might do better if half the fleet weren't sitting on the other side of the map.

I'm using the Hegemony as a benchmark because they're fun, unique, and challenging to fight, and their builds have clear thought put into them. You can totally see a shell-shocked AI War veteran demanding that the Legion mount Sabots in every available slot, and then you can get mad at him when it charges your shiny new Paragon and depletes its fortress shield in an instant, and then you can figure out that they didn't plan to ever fight an Onslaught that can put its shields down, tank the sabot spam and keep ticking, or an Executor that can cut it down from out of Sabot range. I'd like every faction to feel designed, in the same way.

Utility:

This mod allows players to test their modded factions and equipment against the ones in the base game, or against each other. Do your custom ships' drawbacks really balance out against their advantages? Run this script, and find out empirically!

It also allows enterprising modders to try to balance out the vanilla factions. Can you tweak Tri-Tachyon's AI to make it less of a pushover? How about the League - it's supposed to be able to hold its own against the Hegemony! This lets you verify your changes.

Code:

Code is attached below. I should note that, despite my efforts, something was still bleeding memory, though not enough to preclude a five hour run on my old laptop. I may have fixed in my last set of changes, but keep an eye on performance.

You should run through the .sh file in the mod directory, which changes some settings to facilitate reliability. It does also run just fine from the main executable, though, if you don't feel like doing that, or you forget.
